citation.authors: Vachon CM, Modchalingam S, 't Hart BM, Henriques DYP
citation.title: The effect of age on visuomotor learning processes

study.eligibility_rationale: Upper-extremity centre-out reaching with a 30° rotated cursor, comparing older and younger adults, with reach deviations during the rotated training block and no-cursor reach aftereffects: "Both older (n = 38) and younger (n = 42) adults adapted to a 30˚ visuomotor rotation in a centre-out reaching task." Adaptation during perturbation is reported ("reach deviations during the first three reach training trials, second set of three trials and the final set of 15 trials of the 90 trials in the initial rotated-cursor training task") and aftereffects are reported ("significant reach aftereffects of approximately 15˚ did emerge"). Paper is in English.
study.design_notes: Between-subject 2 (age) x 2 (instruction) design; instruction was manipulated between participants, so instructed and non-instructed arms are independent samples and are listed as two datasets. All participants first completed an aligned (baseline) session and then a single rotated (30° CW) session, so the rotated training block is the first and only exposure to the perturbation; reach and localization measures are all baseline-corrected against the aligned session. Design trap 1 (repeated exposure): within the rotated session each block of four tasks was repeated four times ("Each block of tasks was repeated four times in each session"), with 30-trial top-up training between tasks; late adaptation should be taken from the initial 90-trial rotated training task (final set of trials 76-90, Fig 3B/3E) rather than later top-ups. Design trap 2 (context change between phases): no-cursor reaches were performed twice, once "No-Cursor with Strategy" and once "No-Cursor without Strategy", with order "counterbalanced between and within each consecutive participant"; only the without-strategy no-cursor reaches match the protocol's aftereffect definition (perturbation and feedback removed, implicit recalibration), the with-strategy block adds an explicit instruction change. Hand localization (active/passive, Fig 5) is a perceptual estimate, not a protocol outcome. Design trap 3 (n discrepancies): Methods gives "Forty-one younger ... and thirty-eight older ... adults were recruited" and four group ns summing to 41 younger + 38 older, and states 4 younger and 3 older were excluded; the Abstract instead reports "older (n = 38) and younger (n = 42)", and degrees of freedom differ again (between-subjects ANOVAs use F(1,75), i.e. 79 participants; localization t-tests use t(35) for older and t(41) for younger). The group-level ns reported in Methods are recorded here and the discrepancy is flagged.

datasets.notes: Late adaptation: baseline-corrected reach deviations in the final trial set (trials 76-90) of the initial 90-trial rotated training task, Fig 3B/3E ("by the last trial set, all groups attained near perfect compensation (reach deviations of roughly 30˚)"); larger deviation toward 30° = more adaptation. Aftereffect: baseline-corrected no-cursor reach deviations in the without-strategy sub-task, Fig 4 left side ("The no-cursor reaches without strategy reflect implicit learning (involuntary reach aftereffects)"); larger = more implicit recalibration. Values appear only in figures in this paper; numeric group means may need the OSF data/R notebook.

study.notes: No tables are present in the paper; all group-level outcome values are shown graphically (Figs 3-5) with statistics reported in text, so a numeric extraction pass will likely need the OSF dataset/R notebook rather than figure reading. Participant-count discrepancy to flag: Methods group ns sum to 41 younger + 38 older (=79, consistent with F(1,75) between-subjects df), while the Abstract states "older (n = 38) and younger (n = 42)" and localization t-tests report t(35) (older) and t(41) (younger). Exclusions are described as "We excluded 4 younger (all from the non-instructed group) and 3 older (1 non-instructed, 2 instructed) participants", with excluded data "never fully pre-processed and hence not statistically analyzed". Reach deviations are measured at maximum velocity for training trials and at reach endpoint for no-cursor trials.
